text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
*The restructuring of the pulp and paper sector will not be completed until the end of September due to lingering disagreements amongst some of the participants.
*Pilots of state airline TAP-Air Portugal contacted North American trade union AFL/CIO for information on the launching of a management buyout of TAP.
*Oil companies are disputing the increase in tax on fuel products' tax saying that it will cost them five to six billion escudos a year.

*According to a study by Salomon Brothers on Banco Comercial Portugues, this institution will buy the remaining shares in Bank Portugues do Atlantico held by Imperio by June 1998 to take its stake to near 100 percent.

*Construction companies Engil, Somague, Soares da Costa and A. Silva & Silva will have more profits in 1997 and 1998 than expected, a market analyst told the paper. Engil is expected to be the one with best performance, with a net profit of 2.35 billion escudos for 1997, and 2.94 for 1998.
*German pharmaceuticals group Boehringer Ingelheim intends to build a new factory in Portugal for the packaging of medicines, chairman Heribert Johann told the paper.
